newsitem.title: USA: Enron on track on EPS growth target.
newsitem.headline: Enron on track on EPS growth target.

text.p: Enron Corp's units made solid contributions to the energy company's higher earnings for the first quarter and the company remains on track to achieve a target of 10 to 15 percent growth in earnings per share this year, Kenneth Lay, chairman and chief executive officer, said Friday.

At the same time, Enron made "significant progress," in its new businesses, both in the U.S. and abroad, he said. He cited as examples the development of a 790-megawatt power station in Sutton Bridge in the United Kingdom and the start of production of offshore natural gas in India.

On projects by the company's gas pipeline group, Lay said the company hopes that the U.S. Federal Energy Regulation Comission will soon approve its northern border pipeline expansion project. The project would bring 700 million cubic feet per day of new Canadian supplies to the midwestern U.S.

On international ventures, Lay said the company continues to make "excellent progress" in developing its $20 billion backlog of energy projects. Over $3 billion of the projects are currently under construction, he said.
Enron is an integrated natural gas and electricity company with assets of about $16 billion.
